t: Kartli, the ancient kingdom of eastern Georgia, ruled from Mtskheta and later Tbilisi, and called Iberia by Greeks and Romans.
It guarded the passes of the Caucasus and balanced for centuries between Rome and Persia as client of one or the other.
It adopted Christianity in the 4th century and produced the earliest Georgian inscriptions and literature.
dyk: Pompey the Great fought his way into Iberia in 65 BCE while chasing Mithridates VI of Pontus, defeating King Artoces in battles on the Mtkvari and Aragvi rivers.
ev: Pharnavaz I unites Kartli, according to Georgian tradition
Pompey invades Iberia and forces King Artoces to submit
Pharasmanes I seizes Armenia for his brother Mithridates
Vespasian fortifies Mtskheta for King Mithridates of Iberia
King Mirian III adopts Christianity through the mission of St Nino
Vakhtang I Gorgasali joins the Armenian revolt against Persia
Hormizd IV abolishes the Iberian monarchy
